newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada makes good on Canadian Air tax break.
newsitem.headline: Canada makes good on Canadian Air tax break.

text.p: The Canadian government on Wednesday made good on its offer to contribute to Canadian Airlines Corp's survival plan by announcing C$20 million per year in fuel tax rebates.
Ottawa agreed to the concession in late November as the struggling carrier attempted to gain wage concessions from unions representing most of its 16,400 employees as part of major restructuring.

Under the program, airlines operating in Canada will be eligible for a rebate for up to C$20 million annually for federal excise taxes paid on aviation fuel in exchange for giving up the right to claim losses against income subject to tax, Canada's finance ministry said.
However, carriers must give up the right to C$10 of their accumulated tax losses for each C$1 of rebate received, instead of C$15.

The provinces of Alberta and British Columbia have also agreed to cuts in fuel taxes. The tax breaks, combined with a sliding-scale system of employee wage cuts, are aimed at adding C$70 million a year to Canadian's bottom line.

The total survival strategy, which also includes an overhaul of the carrier's route network and cuts in management and computer fees paid to one-third owner Amercian Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, is projected to save Canadian C$180 million a year over four years.
Canadian, which has not posted an annual profit this decade, said in November that it faced financial failure unless all parts of the plan fell into place.
The airline is also seeking to defer debt and lease payment obligations to its 70 creditors.
